newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: SOCCER-MARADONA PRAISES BEN JOHNSON FOR GETTING HIM FIT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MARADONA PRAISES BEN JOHNSON FOR GETTING HIM FIT.

text.p: A slim-looking Diego Maradona, appearing fitter than he has done for months, said on Sunday he has lost 11 kilograms (24.2 pounds) since he started training with the disgraced Canadian sprinter Ben Johnson a month ago.

Maradona, 36, attended a news conference at a Buenos Aires hotel along with Johnson and said he was ready for what will be his fourth -- and final -- comeback attempt and expected to return to action for Boca Juniors against Racing Club next Sunday.
To prove his new-found fitness, he ran on a specially-installed treadmill and said he had lost 11 kgs under Johnson's strict control to weigh in at 77 kgs (169.7 pounds/12 stone 12 lbs).
Johnson, who was stripped of the Olympic 100 metres title in Seoul in 1988 after testing positive for the steroid stanozolol, was with Maradona at the presentation.
Maradona said: "I'm coming back because I want to be a champion with Boca. I'm doing it because Giannina asks me: 'Daddy, when are you going to play like in the video games again?'", Maradona said.

Maradona also found time to put in a word for Johnson, who is currently appealing against a life-ban from athletics following a second doping infringement when he returned to the sport after serving a four-year ban for his infamous positive test in 1988.
"I pray to God that...the judges pardon Ben. He's got so much talent. He's an animal," Maradona said.
Maradona signed a contract with Boca Juniors in April but has yet to play for the club and will only be paid on a match-by-match basis.
Maradona's last comeback with Boca fizzled out when he stopped going to training, due to a lack of motivation compounded by a well-known appetite for pizza.
His comeback before that one ended in disgrace when he failed a dope test and was kicked out of the 1994 World Cup finals in the United States.

Maradona, who for much of the 1980s was regarded as the world's best footballer and led Argentina to victory in the 1986 World Cup finals, has been battling against a variety of problems for the last few years.

And there are continuing doubts about his health that have dogged him since he admitted he was a cocaine addict. Maradona went to hospital for high blood pressure checks in April and fell ill in Chile, breaking out in a cold sweat on television after dancing with a former Miss Universe.

His recent career has been blighted by drugs, bans, failed comebacks and attempts at coaching. A proposed final lucrative transfer to Japan to finish what might be left of his playing career also came to nothing earlier this year.

Maradona's most recent playing performance was on April 27 when he played for an hour for a Rest of the World team against a European Select XI in Barcelona. He played for an hour and although he showed flashes of his old skill, he also looked very overweight.
